race_context: The 'Tipton Community School Board' seats belong to Tipton Community School Corporation (TCSC) in Tipton, Tipton County, which runs Tipton Elementary, Tipton Middle and Tipton High School {tcsc_vote}{nces_tcsc}. Federal data list 1,366 students in 2024-25, and the district says enrollment has declined gradually over the past decade {nces_tcsc}{tcsc_ref_why}. Scott Jaworski became superintendent on July 1, 2026, succeeding the retired Ryan Glaze; the board chose him in 2025 and he served as associate superintendent and then interim superintendent during the transition {rep_supt_20260707}{kt_supt_2025}{rep_brief_20260609}.

The board has seven members: Rob Cochrane (president), Jennifer Humrichous (vice president), Kimberly Fague (secretary), Tami Brown, Andrea Campbell, Eric Underwood and Beth Woelfert {tcsc_board}{rep_brief_20260113}. Members are elected from residence areas that include the City of Tipton and Cicero Township; the district site does not describe the full seat plan {tcsc_board}{kt_forum_2022}{kt_kyc_2024}.

Cicero Township: Robert Cochrane won this seat unopposed in 2022 and is running again, unopposed {kt_results_2022}{in_list}. Cicero Township has a second seat, filled by Beth Woelfert in the 2024 election, which is not on the 2026 ballot {kt_kyc_2024}{kt_newmembers_2025}.

City of Tipton — likely two seats, not one: in 2022 voters filled two City of Tipton seats, electing Jason Springer and Eric Underwood and unseating incumbent Chris McNew {kt_forum_2022}{kt_results_2022}. Springer resigned in September 2024, and the board interviewed six people in November 2024 to serve the rest of his term; it appointed Tamera Brown and Kimberly Fague to fill vacancies in late 2024 {kt_vacancy_2024}{kt_newmembers_2025}. Both 2022 City seats would normally be up in 2026, but the state list shows this race as 'vote for 1'; this guide could not confirm the number of seats from an official 2026 ballot {in_list}.

Incumbents running: Cochrane (Cicero Township) and Eric Underwood (City of Tipton) are current members on the ballot; Tamera Noble Brown appears to be the board member listed as Tami Brown, who was appointed in late 2024, though no fetched source gives her full name {in_list}{tcsc_board}{kt_newmembers_2025}.
Party labels: the state list shows Cochrane, Underwood and Tamera Noble Brown with the Republican label, Caiden C. McNew as Democratic and Christopher K. McNew as Independent {in_list}.

Operating referendum on the same ballot: on June 30, 2026 the board approved placing the district's first operating referendum on the November 3 ballot, asking for a tax rate of up to $0.25 per $100 of assessed value for up to eight years, raising no more than $2 million a year {rep_ref_20260708}{tcsc_ref}. The district estimates the cost for a median home at $174 to $216 a year and about $4 per acre of farmland, and says the money would go to academic programs, student supports, staff recruitment and retention, transportation and operations, not construction or athletic facilities {rep_ref_20260708}{tcsc_ref}.

Budget and SEA 1: the district cites revenue losses from the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1), property-tax cap (circuit breaker) losses, rising costs and declining enrollment, and says earlier cuts — staff reductions through attrition, shared positions, deferred maintenance and transportation changes — cannot fully close the gap; it says cuts to staffing, programs, transportation and student services may follow if the referendum fails {tcsc_ref_why}{tcsc_ref_faq}{tcsc_ref}. The district's pages do not give a dollar figure for the SEA 1 loss {tcsc_ref_why}{tcsc_ref_faq}.

Fees: in January 2026 the board approved transportation participation fees to offset SEA 1 costs, including a fixed fee for extracurricular activities and a field trip fee; in July 2026 it kept the transportation fee at $5 per student per round trip, to be reviewed in June 2027 {rep_brief_20260113}{rep_brief_20260711}. Meal prices rise for 2026-27 to meet a required weighted average {rep_brief_20260609}.

Facilities: a Tipton Elementary playground replacement was funded in part by a $200,000 Tipton County Foundation grant; in January 2026 the board put off a $2.95 million microturbine energy project, saying the upfront cost was not feasible {rep_brief_20260113}{rep_brief_20260609}.

Other 2026 actions: the board adopted 2026 legislative policy updates including wireless device restrictions (June 2026) and set a 2027 budget hearing for September 22 with adoption scheduled for October 13, 2026 {rep_brief_20260609}{rep_brief_20260711}.

Forums: no 2026 candidate forum was found for this guide. In a 2022 Tipton County Chamber of Commerce forum, Underwood and Chris McNew (then the incumbent) answered questions on teacher retention and district programs {kt_forum_2022}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board president, running unopposed for the Cicero Township seat he first won unopposed in 2022 {in_list}{kt_results_2022}{rep_brief_20260113}.
background: Elected to the Cicero Township seat in 2022 without opposition and joined the board in January 2023 {kt_results_2022}.
Board president; re-elected to that post at the January 13, 2026 reorganization {rep_brief_20260113}{tcsc_board}.
path_to_ballot: Listed with the Republican label on the state candidate list; he is the only candidate for the seat {in_list}.

items: As president he leads the board that approved the June 30, 2026 operating referendum resolution; no vote tally or individual statement was published in the coverage reviewed {rep_ref_20260708}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. On the superintendent transition approved in 2025, he told the Kokomo Tribune, "I didn't want to do anything to disrupt that," referring to the year-long transition from Ryan Glaze to Scott Jaworski {kt_supt_2025}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent; elected to a City of Tipton seat in 2022 and seeking reelection {kt_results_2022}{tcsc_board}{in_list}.
background: Former teacher who taught at Southwood for five years before leaving the profession, and a relatively new Tipton resident as of 2022, according to the Kokomo Tribune {kt_forum_2022}.
Won one of two City of Tipton seats in 2022 with about 27 percent of the vote in a four-candidate field {kt_results_2022}.
path_to_ballot: Listed with the Republican label on the state candidate list {in_list}.

items: In 2022 he said the district should survey teachers, students and community members, including teachers who leave and families who choose other districts or choose Tipton {kt_forum_2022}.

Explaining his own departure from teaching in 2022, he said, "I think I left for the same reason a lot of people leave jobs, that is the culture and leadership," adding that pay was not the reason {kt_forum_2022}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and serves on board advisory committees {tcsc_board}{rep_brief_20260711}. No 2026 statement from him on the board's record, including the referendum, was found.
